title: White rice with vegetables and cheese and/or cream sauce, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of boiled white rice, sautéed vegetables (such as carrots, broccoli, bell pepper) and a sauce made from cheese and/or cream with added fat. It combines carbohydrates, vegetable vitamins and minerals, as well as saturated fats that give the dish a creamy texture and rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is a primary source of energy due to its high starch content.
Vegetables retain most of their vitamins and fiber when steamed or quickly stir‑fried.
Cheese and cream add not only taste but also calcium, important for bone health.
The added fat enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) from the vegetables.
The dish is common in Asian and Mediterranean cuisines as a hearty lunch or dinner.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Rice provides a rapid source of glucose needed for maintaining energy levels.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Vegetables are rich in vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, and potassium, supporting immunity and heart function.

items.title: Calcium from cheese and cream
items.content: Calcium is essential for bone and tooth health and participates in muscle contraction.

items.title: Fat for better nutrient absorption
items.content: Saturated and monounsaturated fats help the body absorb fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Cheese and a modest amount of cream contribute dairy protein, aiding tissue repair.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The dish contains a notable amount of fats and carbs, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese and cream may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: If the sauce is seasoned with salt, the dish can be high in sodium, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cheese or cream.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, often as a main course. It pairs well with fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or soy sauce for extra flavor. For added protein, include chicken breast or tofu.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. When reheating, add a splash of water or milk to prevent the sauce from becoming too thick.
